messages.content: 请检索以下问题的相关原文：关于论文《A Readable Read: Automatic Assessment of Language Learning Materials based on Linguistic Complexity》，what linguistics features did they apply?

claims.text: 该论文的特征集基于既有文献和一本面向瑞典语二语学习者的语法书构建，分为五个子组：长度特征、词汇特征、形态特征、句法特征和语义特征。
长度特征（Len）包括以词元数计的句子长度、以字符数计的句子长度、超长词（长度超过十三个字符）以及传统的瑞典语可读性公式 LIX。
词汇特征（Lex）利用 Kelly 词表（一种提供每个词元的 CEFR 等级和频率的词汇资源），以每千词的出现率（IncSc）而非百分比来度量：包括各 CEFR 等级词语的出现率、高于文本或句子 CEFR 等级的难词、不在 Kelly 词表中的词元、未找到对应词元的词元，以及平均对数频率。
形态特征（Morph）包括各词类及其变体的出现率，标点、小品词、从属连词和并列连词的出现率，细致屈折信息（如中性性别名词的出现率以及不同动词形式与全部动词之比），双对数和平方根类型-词元比（而非简单 TTR），名词比率，代词与介词之比，两个词汇密度特征，以及关系结构特征。
句法特征（Synt）部分基于依存弧的长度（深度）和方向，并辅以分裂句中关系从句的出现率以及前置和后置修饰语（如形容词和介词短语）的出现率。
语义特征（Sem）基于瑞典语词汇语义资源 SALDO，使用每个词元的平均义项数以及每个名词的平均名词义项数。
在句子层面，使用多种特征组合相比仅使用词汇特征使分类准确率提高了 7%；而在文档层面，词汇特征更具主导性，仅用词频特征几乎与全部特征组合同样具有预测力。

claims.text: This paper is the first approach for predicting linguistic complexity for Swedish second-language learning material on a 5-point scale.
The supervised machine learning model is based on a range of linguistic features and the paper first shows that the traditional Swedish readability measure LIX is not suitable for this task.

The linguistic features explored for readability tasks incorporate information, among others, from part-of-speech (POS) taggers and dependency parsers, and cognitively motivated features have also been proposed, for example in Coh-Metrix.
The document-level model achieved an accuracy of 81.3% and an F-score of 0.8.
A separate model trained on sentence-level data with five classes yielded 63.4% accuracy, and an adjacent accuracy of 92% was achieved.
Using a combination of different features, compared to using lexical features alone, resulted in a 7% improvement in classification accuracy at the sentence level.
At the document level, lexical features were more dominant.

Using only word-frequency features was almost as predictive as a combination of all features for the document level, but the combination made more accurate predictions for sentences, resulting in a 7% difference in accuracy.
The authors found that taking into consideration multiple linguistic dimensions when assessing linguistic complexity is especially useful for sentence-level analysis.

Compared to LIX, the document-level model achieved a substantial gain in both accuracy and F-score (46% and 0.6 higher respectively), and at the sentence level the complete feature set performed 23% and 22% above the majority baseline and LIX respectively.
LIX combines the average number of words per sentence in the text with the percentage of long words, i.e. tokens consisting of more than six characters.
